newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber rallies limit on short covering.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber rallies limit on short covering.

text.p: CME lumber futures continued to trade erratically and ran up for a limit gain of $10.00 per tbf in November after closing sharply lower Tuesday and briefly posting a limit loss. Short covering and some new buying pushed prices up into buy stops, traders said.
November posted a limit gain at $352.20 per tbf and then slipped to trade $9.20 higher at $351.40 per tbf. January was up $7.50 at $362.00 and other months were up $6.10 to $4.30 early.

Lumber futures have swung sharply since late last week when they established a chart support level near $340.00, basis November. Buying by Prudential Securities and Smith Barney prompted local buying and futures ran up into the stops, traders said.
Demand came despite continued weakness in cash lumber prices. Random Lengths early Wednesday quoted cash spruce at $392, down $18 from Friday and down $38 from last week.
